parts/windows.mjs now builds clean: the oriel calls and pane re-set write through a view that only touches air or this part's own glass, so the six REFUSED writes are gone and there is no OFF-PALETTE report.
The six refusals came from the roof, not an earlier windows write: its soffit course sits at z 20, y 21 across the oriel tops, so x 6, 10, 14, 18 were already the same stone and x 8, 16 were roof stone where glass was wanted.
make.sh produced build.nbt (grid 30x36x29, 177 windows-and-doors cells placed).

waste.what: Traced which part owned six refused cells by dumping per-part cell lists to a temp file, then checking sockets reservations and the roof's placements by hand, one node probe at a time.

waste.tool: The REFUSED line should name the owner, e.g. 'owned by roof (laid after shell)', and parts-report.json should list roof cells as their own entry. waste.cost: one node script over x 3..26 for 5 rows
waste.tool: `mcd render`/`mcd zoom` on the z 20 face, or a `mcd plan`-style text grid of one plane, would show the clash directly.
